children: By Sukanya Mitra and Rajendra Jadhav
Gold demand in India improved this week as a drop in prices spurred some buying interest, while investment flows continued to support consumption in top consumer China despite slow jewellery sales.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi reiterated on Tuesday that people should refrain from buying gold unless necessary, making a similar appeal in May, after which the country raised import duties on gold and silver to 15% from an earlier 6%.
"Buyers had been on the sidelines, hoping for an import duty cut, but Modi’s remarks on gold buying put that speculation to rest,” a Chennai-based bullion dealer said.
Dealers quoted a discount (XAU-IN-PREM) of up to $54 an ounce over official domestic prices this week, inclusive of 15% import and 3% sales levies, a drop from last week’s discount of up to $135.
Domestic gold prices (MAUc1) were around 155,300 rupees ($1,640) per 10 grams on Friday after rising to 164,773 rupees last week, the highest since early March.

"The price volatility is confusing buyers. Prices need to stabilise ahead of the upcoming festivals so buyers can make purchases with confidence,” a Mumbai-based bullion dealer with a private bank said.
In China, bullion (XAU-CN-PREM) traded at premiums of $3.5-$9 an ounce to the global benchmark price, compared with discounts of $2-$5 last week.

"China's gold premium is proving more resilient than headline price action suggests. Despite rising yields, a stronger dollar, persistent inflation concerns and increasing expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening, physical demand remains intact," said Bernard Sin, regional director, Greater China at MKS PAMP.
International spot gold prices were on track for a weekly gain.
"Retail investment, institutional and official-sector demand remain strong, while jewellery demand continues to struggle under the weight of high prices," independent analyst Ross Norman said.
In Singapore (XAU-SG-PREM), gold was sold between a $1 discount and a premium of $2 this week, while in Hong Kong (XAU-HK-PREM) it traded at premiums of $0.5 to $1.5.
Meanwhile, in Japan (XAU-TK-PREM), gold was sold between a $0.25 discount and a $0.5 premium.
